questions.solution_text:
$m_{PQ}=\dfrac{2-(-2)}{1-(-1)}$
$=2$
$m_{QR}=\dfrac{0-2}{5-1}$
$=-\dfrac{1}{2}$
$m_{PQ}\times m_{QR}=2\times\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$
$=-1$
$PQ\perp QR$, so the right angle is at $Q$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{midpoint }EG=\left(\dfrac{-2+3}{2},\dfrac{-1+2}{2}\right)$
$=\left(\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$
$\text{midpoint }FH=\left(\dfrac{2+(-1)}{2},\dfrac{-2+3}{2}\right)$
$=\left(\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$
The diagonals share a midpoint, so they bisect each other and $EFGH$ is a parallelogram.

questions.solution_text:
For a parallelogram $ABCD$, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ share a midpoint.
$\text{midpoint }AC=\left(\dfrac{-2+5}{2},\dfrac{1+3}{2}\right)$
$=\left(\dfrac{3}{2},2\right)$
Let $D=(x,y)$.
$\left(\dfrac{2+x}{2},\dfrac{-1+y}{2}\right)=\left(\dfrac{3}{2},2\right)$
$\dfrac{2+x}{2}=\dfrac{3}{2}$
$x=1$
$\dfrac{-1+y}{2}=2$
$y=5$
$D=(1,5)$

All four sides are equal, so $ABCD$ is at least a rhombus.
$AC=\sqrt{(-2-2)^2+(-1-1)^2}$
$=\sqrt{20}$
$BD=\sqrt{(1-(-1))^2+(-2-2)^2}$
$=\sqrt{20}$
The diagonals are equal, so the rhombus has right angles.
A rhombus with equal diagonals is a square, so $ABCD$ is a square.
